# Hybrid Surface-Volume and Mesh Representation

Also called: Hybrid Neural Representations, Implicit-Explicit NeRF Hybrids

## Overview
This family integrates explicit geometric primitives or implicit surface fields with [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) to decouple geometry reconstruction from appearance modeling. It addresses the slow convergence and ambiguous geometry of pure volumetric NeRFs by using surface boundaries to guide sampling and define radiance evaluation points.

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Neural Surfel Radiance Fields](7358-neural-surfel-radiance-fields.md)
Represents scenes as a dynamic set of neural surfels (position, normal, radius, neural features) and uses differentiable [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) for online integration. It distinguishes itself by using explicit surfel primitives with learned features rather than implicit occupancy fields, enabling [fast rendering](#11491-interactive-forward-rendering-with-approximate-splatting.md) without per-scene optimization. Choose this for large-scale, dynamic indoor scenes requiring incremental updates.

### [Unified Neural Implicit Surface and Radiance Field Rendering](9732-unified-neural-implicit-surface-and-radiance-field-rendering.md)
Replaces volume density with a continuous occupancy field $o_\theta$ where the zero-level set defines the surface. It unifies [surface rendering with volume](#2614-surface-rendering-pipeline.md) rendering by finding surface intersections via root-finding and sampling densely only near the surface with a decaying interval schedule. Choose this for high-precision static reconstruction where [mesh extraction](#14720-mesh-extraction.md) is required without per-pixel masks.

### [NeuMesh++](11394-neumesh.md)
[Encodes scene](#17508-encode-scene.md) geometry and appearance into disentangled latent codes anchored to the vertices of a mesh scaffold. It solves high-frequency detail preservation and efficient fine-grained editing in unbounded scenes by using a local space parameterization and hybrid blending with an implicit hash grid for backgrounds. Choose this for unbounded scenes requiring editable mesh geometry and per-vertex latent codes.

### [Structured Latent Codes Anchored to Mesh](12715-structured-latent-codes-anchored-to-mesh.md)
Stores geometry and appearance latent codes at anchor nodes (typically mesh vertices) on a deformable mesh, enabling local editing and deformation tracking. It differs from implicit surface methods by using explicit mesh topology to define spatial relationships and resolves surface-normal ambiguity via a signed height indicator. Choose this for scenarios requiring local editing and deformation tracking of explicit mesh structures.

### DoubleField
#### definition
- [S1] A framework combining surface field and radiance field for high-fidelity human reconstruction and rendering, bridging them via a shared feature embedding and [surface-guided sampling strategy](#7324-sdf-guided-sampling.md).
- [S1] The core representation is a joint implicit function $f_{db}$ that bridges the surface field and the radiance field, allowing shared learning space for geometry and radiance reconstruction.
#### step
- [S1] Build associations between surface and radiance fields using a feature embedding shared by these fields in the network architecture.
- [S1] Apply a surface-guided sampling strategy to disentangle the geometry component from the appearance modeling.
#### parameter
- [S1] Input resolution: Ultra-high resolution images, e.g., 4K, are used as input to the method.
#### comparison
- [S1] Unlike PIFu which isolates geometry and texture making texture learning space discontinuous, DoubleField enables joint implicit function learning.
- [S1] Unlike [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) which entangles density and color leading to inconsistent geometry with sparse views, DoubleField imposes geometry constraints on the radiance field.

## Background
DoubleField was introduced to bridge surface and radiance fields for high-fidelity human reconstruction [S1]. The family builds on [Neural Radiance Fields](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) by introducing geometric priors to guide [radiance field optimization](#44-radiance-field-optimization.md).
